title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
one_line_claim: SnapKV compresses KV caches by identifying and retaining only important token positions per attention head, achieving 3.6x faster generation and 8.2x memory efficiency on 16K tokens with negligible accuracy loss.
method_summary: SnapKV analyzes attention patterns in an observation window at the end of prompts to identify which positions each attention head attends to. Selects clustered important KV positions for each head via voting on attention weights, clusters surrounding features, and stores only these compressed KVs for generation. Requires no fine-tuning.

key_findings.finding: Each attention head consistently focuses on specific prompt features during generation; the last input window matches actual generation attention patterns.
key_findings.quote: We discover that each attention head in the model consistently focuses on specific prompt attention features during generation... the last window of input sequence recognizes highly similar attention allocation pattern with the actual generation.

key_findings.finding: SnapKV achieves 3.6x increase in decoding speed and 8.2x memory efficiency on 16K token inputs.
key_findings.quote: SnapKV achieves a consistent decoding speed with a 3.6x increase in generation speed and an 8.2x enhancement in memory efficiency compared to the baseline when processing inputs of 16K tokens.

key_findings.finding: Processes up to 380K context tokens on a single A100-80GB GPU with negligible accuracy drop on Needle-in-a-Haystack.
key_findings.quote: SnapKV can process up to 380K context tokens on a single A100-80GB GPU using HuggingFace implementation with minor changes, exhibiting only a negligible accuracy drop in the Needle-in-a-Haystack test.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both operate on compressed KV caches during generation and work with per-token information without model fine-tuning. SnapKV is a compression press HERALD evaluates.
differs_on: SnapKV predicts which tokens to retain based on static attention patterns; HERALD predicts when compression-induced catastrophic failures will occur using dynamic logit features.
SnapKV is a compression method that reduces memory and compute; HERALD is a hazard detector forecasting failures caused by compression.
SnapKV uses attention weight voting and clustering; HERALD uses XGBoost on logit-derived features.
